generalfeedback: To solve this problem you will need to use the chain rule calc_chain_rule and the quotient rule calc_quotient_rule. Let \[f({{CT:0}})={{CT:3}}\] and \[g({{CT:0}})={{CT:1}}.\] Then \(f({{CT:0}})=[g({{CT:0}})]^{{CT:2}}\). So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:3}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{dx} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}[g^{{CT:2}}]\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[g] \end{array}\] In order to find \(\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}\) you have to define two new functions: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:4}}\) and \(i({{CT:0}})={{CT:5}}\). So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}(g) &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left(\frac{h}{i}\right) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{\frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot i - h\cdot \frac{di}{d{{CT:0}}}}{i^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{\left[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:4}})\right]\cdot ({{CT:5}}) - ({{CT:4}})\cdot \left[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:5}})\right]}{({{CT:5}})^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{[{{CT:6}}]\cdot ({{CT:5}}) - ({{CT:4}})\cdot [{{CT:7}}]}{{CT:8}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:8}}. \end{array}\] Now, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}[g^{{CT:2}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:2}}g^{{CT:10}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:11}} \end{array}\] Hence, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:3}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}[g^{{CT:2}}]\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[g] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:8}}\cdot {{CT:11}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array}\]
